sections.html:
Faribault is the Rice County seat, about 50 miles south of Minneapolis and Saint Paul, where the Straight and Cannon Rivers meet. Population is 25,040 as of July 2025, up 2.3 percent from 2020. Interstate 35 runs along the western edge, and Minnesota Highways 3, 21 and 60 serve the city.

Owner-occupied houses here carry a typical value of $241,500, and two out of three households (66.1 percent) own their homes. Monthly rent is $1,074. The city counts 8,938 households of 2.48 people each, with income at $61,449 and a drive to work of 19.0 minutes.

Faribault is an older city, and many properties carry decades of ownership history. Ask for the title search and a fresh survey early. Write down when the house was built and when the big updates happened, since buyers always ask and a ready answer keeps things moving.

Prices here are modest, so a big repair eats a large slice of what the house will fetch. A new roof or foundation fix hurts more in Faribault than in a suburb where houses cost two or three times as much. Many owners put the repair bill next to an as-is offer before choosing.

Cold winters mean inspectors go over the roof, gutters and basement with care, so hang on to receipts for recent work. Trails help the pitch too: the Sakatah Singing Hills State Trail starts here and runs to Mankato, and Central Avenue has restored historic storefronts.

sections.h2: What you must disclose in writing
sections.html:
Your basic obligation is in Section 513.55 and reaches every material fact you know about. Radon falls under Section 144.496, wells under Section 103I.235 and sewage under Section 115.55.

Wells come up at the county recorder. A transfer that needs a value certificate also needs well information, and the deed for a lot with no well has to say so. Filing a well disclosure certificate costs $54, and the Health Department's database, or 800-383-9808, shows whether one is already on file.

sections.h2: Keeping it as a rental or letting go
sections.html:
Every residential rental in Faribault must be registered, hold a city rental license and pass inspection. A July 2022 ordinance update ended the requirement that landlords run criminal background checks, though the city still recommends them. It also confirmed an occupancy limit of no less than two times the number of legal bedrooms plus one, with children under age two not counted.

Owners and managers of one or more rental units must hold Crime Free Multi-Housing Phase I certification before a rental license renews. The Building Code Division is at 208 First Avenue NW, phone 507-333-0359, and the rental division takes email at rental@ci.faribault.mn.us.

Training, registration and inspections can be a lot for a house you inherited or left behind. Selling skips all three, and a cash buyer does not ask you to complete them first.

Payments go to the Property Tax and Elections Office on the second floor of the Government Services Building, 320 Third Street NW. Bills of $100 or less for the whole year are due in full on the first date.

Rice County property tax payment dates
Property classFirst installmentSecond installment
Non-agricultural real propertyMay 15October 15
Agricultural real propertyMay 15November 15
Personal propertyMay 15None
Mobile homeAugust 31November 15

Behind on taxes? Ask that office for a payoff figure, and your closing agent can settle the balance out of your sale money.

When renters live in the house, hand the lease to the buyer and the closing agent early. The occupancy limit and inspection rules follow the property, so whoever keeps it as a rental takes over registration and certification. Once the house is empty, let the rental division know. A cash buyer can take the house with tenants still there or after they leave, whichever you agree on.

Rice County asks for two checks, both payable to the county, when a deed is submitted. One pays recorder fees. The other pays deed tax and mortgage registration tax, which the tax office takes in. The deed tax rate is 0.33 percent (Section 287.21), and the auditor receives the value certificate required by Section 272.115. Reach the recorder at 507-332-6114.

The closing agent usually files the deed. Check your purchase agreement to see who pays each fee.

• List with an agent: fits a house in good shape when you can sit through showings and wait for a buyer's mortgage.
  • Sell it yourself: you set the price, host the showings and write up the contract.
  • Cash buyer, as is: popular for inherited houses, rentals with open violations and homes whose repairs would outrun what a retail buyer pays.

Get a written estimate from each, then take off commissions, repairs and carrying costs to see your take-home.

Keep one folder for the sale. Drop in the newest tax statement, a survey if you own one, the well certificate, receipts for roof, furnace or foundation work, and any tenant lease. A title company will want most of it. Inherited the house? Add the court papers showing who may sign.

Then walk through as a buyer would. Jot down every flaw you know of, from a damp basement corner to a sagging gutter, since the written disclosure covers what you know. Inspectors find most of it regardless.

The steps run like this: ask for an offer, let the buyer see the house as it is, then pick a closing day. The title company searches the record, gathers disclosures and drafts the deed. There is no lender appraisal to wait on, and you do not fix anything first. The closing day bends to your calendar, useful if you are leaving town or wrapping up an estate. On closing day you sign the deed, hand over keys and any garage openers, and receive your proceeds once the title company has paid off the mortgage and any taxes owed. Plan a last walk-through so you know the house is empty and the utilities are squared away. Before closing, confirm any well certificate, pay off taxes owed and gather the keys.

faqs.q: How much is a typical house worth in Faribault?
faqs.a: Owner-occupied homes have a median value of $241,500. Condition and street can push yours higher or lower, so use that number only as a rough guide.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Faribault rental that is behind on its license?
faqs.a: Yes. Write or call the city rental division (rental@ci.faribault.mn.us, 507-333-0359) to find out what is open, and tell the buyer about known problems. Anyone who rents the house next must register it and meet the inspection and certification rules.

faqs.q: Who handles recording a Faribault deed?
faqs.a: The Rice County Recorder at 507-332-6114 records deeds, and deed tax is handled by the Property Tax and Elections office. The county asks for separate checks for recorder fees and for deed tax, both payable to Rice County.

faqs.q: Do I need a well disclosure certificate?
faqs.a: If the property has a known well, yes. If you know of no wells, the deed can carry the statement that the seller does not know of any wells on the property. The county charges $54 to file a certificate.

faqs.q: When are Rice County taxes due?
faqs.a: Non-agricultural real property pays on May 15 and October 15, while agricultural parcels pay on May 15 and November 15. A bill of $100 or less for the year is due entirely on May 15.
